plan: v2.8 44 G7/G8: 20 cases; the origin's version is said in the transcript, the receiver holds a different received version as hearsay, and the last player line invites the receiver to speak of it. Invented names only. {receiver} is the receiver's card name, filled at run time.

cases.subject: the north bridge
cases.origin: the north bridge washed out in the storm
cases.received: soldiers pulled down the north bridge to trap deserters

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: At the well, the miller Hobb tells anyone who will listen that the north bridge washed out in the storm.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I fill my waterskin and nod to {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The square empties as the noon bell rings, and {receiver} lingers by the trough.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, you hear everything in this town. What do you know about the north bridge?

cases.subject: the old well
cases.origin: the old well in the square has gone dry
cases.received: someone poisoned the old well in the square

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A washerwoman named Bessa grumbles at the market that the old well in the square has gone dry.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I buy two apples and toss one to {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Pigeons scatter from the eaves as a cart rolls past the stalls.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, should we fill our skins at the old well before we go?

cases.subject: the mayor
cases.origin: the mayor left for the capital on business
cases.received: the mayor fled the town owing the guild money

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The clerk Odran announces from the hall steps that the mayor left for the capital on business.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I lean on the railing beside {receiver} and watch the crowd.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The crowd drifts back to the stalls, muttering.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, where has the mayor gone, really?

cases.subject: the lighthouse keeper
cases.origin: the lighthouse keeper fell ill with a fever
cases.received: the lighthouse keeper was seen rowing out to a smugglers' ship at night

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: On the quay, the net-mender Pell says the lighthouse keeper fell ill with a fever.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I watch the gulls circle the harbor with {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The tide turns, and the boats knock against the posts.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, the lamp was dark last night. What is going on with the lighthouse keeper?

cases.subject: the barley harvest
cases.origin: the barley harvest came in early this year
cases.received: a blight has rotted half the barley fields

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A farmhand called Tobin boasts in the tavern that the barley harvest came in early this year.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I order two mugs of ale and slide one to {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The fire pops, and a dog stretches out under a bench.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, how is the barley harvest looking out on the farms?

cases.subject: the baker
cases.origin: the baker is closing his shop for the winter
cases.received: the baker was arrested for cutting his flour with chalk

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The cobbler Wenna remarks to a customer that the baker is closing his shop for the winter.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I wait for {receiver} outside the cobbler's door.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Smoke curls from the chimneys along the lane.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, the bakery shutters are down. What happened to the baker?

cases.subject: the spice caravan
cases.origin: the spice caravan is three days late because of mud on the pass
cases.received: bandits took the spice caravan on the pass

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: At the gate, the toll-keeper Brannoc tells the waiting traders that the spice caravan is three days late because of mud on the pass.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I count my coins while {receiver} checks the horses.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A cold wind comes down from the hills, flapping the awnings.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, any word on the spice caravan?

cases.subject: the temple bell
cases.origin: the temple bell cracked when the frost came
cases.received: the priests sold the temple bell to pay a debt

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: An old sexton named Garrow sighs to the passersby that the temple bell cracked when the frost came.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I brush the snow off my cloak and walk on with {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The temple steps are quiet, and no bell marks the hour.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, why has the temple bell gone silent?

cases.subject: the wolf
cases.origin: a lone wolf was seen near the sheep pens
cases.received: a pack of wolves killed four sheep and a dog

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A shepherd boy named Kip tells the village that a lone wolf was seen near the sheep pens.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I tighten my boot laces and look up at {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Mist hangs low over the pasture as evening comes.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, should we worry about the wolf by the sheep pens?

cases.subject: the ferry
cases.origin: the ferry stopped running because the river is too high
cases.received: the ferryman drowned when the ferry overturned

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: At the landing, the rope-maker Ilsa tells travelers that the ferry stopped running because the river is too high.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I set my pack down on the landing next to {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Brown water rushes past the empty posts of the landing.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what do you know about the ferry?

cases.subject: the copper mine
cases.origin: the copper mine shut a tunnel after a small collapse
cases.received: the copper mine struck silver in the deep tunnel

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The foreman Dorrin tells the tavern that the copper mine shut a tunnel after a small collapse.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I trade a joke with {receiver} over the noise of the room.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Miners crowd the bar, their hands black with dust.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what is the news from the copper mine?

cases.subject: the smith's daughter
cases.origin: the smith's daughter is to marry a cooper from the valley
cases.received: the smith's daughter ran off with a traveling actor

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The weaver Annis tells her neighbors that the smith's daughter is to marry a cooper from the valley.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I stop at the forge with {receiver}, but the fire is cold.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The smith hammers nothing today; he sits on the step, staring at the road.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what is the matter with the smith's daughter?

cases.subject: the tax
cases.origin: the new tax collector arrives at midsummer
cases.received: the duke has doubled the salt tax

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A notary named Flint reads from a scroll that the new tax collector arrives at midsummer.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I shoulder through the crowd to stand by {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The merchants frown and return to their counting.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what is all this talk of taxes about?

cases.subject: the tannery
cases.origin: a lamp tipped over in the tannery and scorched a wall
cases.received: the tannery burned down with the winter hides inside

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The tanner's apprentice Rook tells the street that a lamp tipped over in the tannery and scorched a wall.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I wrinkle my nose at the smell of smoke and glance at {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A thin haze still hangs over the east end of town.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what happened at the tannery?

cases.subject: the healer
cases.origin: the healer is gathering herbs in the hills this week
cases.received: the healer was chased out of the village for witchcraft

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The healer's neighbor Sorrel tells a visitor at the door that the healer is gathering herbs in the hills this week.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I rub my sore shoulder and sit down beside {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The healer's garden gate swings on one hinge in the wind.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, my shoulder needs looking at. Where is the healer?

cases.subject: the merchant ship
cases.origin: a merchant ship put into the harbor with a torn sail
cases.received: a merchant ship came in flying a plague flag

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A dockhand named Mabry calls out to the fish sellers that a merchant ship put into the harbor with a torn sail.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I buy a paper of fried fish and share it with {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The harbor master's boat rows out toward the far mooring.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what is the story with that merchant ship out there?

cases.subject: the widow's orchard
cases.origin: the widow Marl is selling her apple orchard
cases.received: the widow Marl found a buried chest of coins under her apple trees

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The carter Hesketh mentions to the inn that the widow Marl is selling her apple orchard.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I warm my hands at the inn fire next to {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Rain taps at the shutters as the evening wears on.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, what is going on with the widow Marl and her orchard?

cases.subject: the guard captain
cases.origin: the guard captain broke his leg falling from his horse
cases.received: the guard captain was stabbed in a tavern brawl

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: A young guard named Corwin tells the gatehouse that the guard captain broke his leg falling from his horse.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I show my pass at the gate and wait for {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The gatehouse is short of men tonight, and the torches burn low.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, why is the guard captain not at his post?

cases.subject: the autumn fair
cases.origin: the autumn fair is moving to the east meadow
cases.received: the autumn fair is cancelled because of the fever in the south

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The crier Ambrose shouts from the fountain that the autumn fair is moving to the east meadow.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I hand {receiver} a ribbon I bought for the fair.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Children run circles around the fountain, singing.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, are we still going to the autumn fair?

cases.subject: the stranger in the grey cloak
cases.origin: a stranger in a grey cloak has taken the room above the stables
cases.received: a stranger in a grey cloak paid the innkeeper with old royal gold

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: The stable girl Linnet whispers to the grooms that a stranger in a grey cloak has taken the room above the stables.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I hang my wet cloak by the door and sit across from {receiver}.

transcript.speaker: narrator
transcript.text: Footsteps creak on the boards overhead and then fall quiet.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: {receiver}, who is the stranger in the grey cloak?
